//: Permissions for the UNATTENDED SEO routines (scripts/seo/run-routine.sh).
Three of them share this list: daily-content, weekly-traffic, news-watch.
A scheduled `claude -p` run is non-interactive: any permission prompt has
nobody to answer it, so the run stalls. The runner uses
--permission-mode dontAsk, which honours these lists and DECLINES anything
not covered rather than blocking forever.
PATTERN SYNTAX — this cost two failed dry runs. A Bash pattern must be the
FULL command prefix followed by `:*`. `Bash(node scripts/seo/:*)` does NOT
match `node scripts/seo/kwstore.mjs stats`; it was silently denied and the
routine aborted at step 0. Each script needs its own entry.
Scoped rather than bypassPermissions on purpose: this routine commits to
master and deploys to production, so it should do exactly that and nothing
else. `pnpm run build` is denied because it runs check-db against the live
production database — the gate is `build-app`.
`git checkout -- src/content/` and `rm src/content/` are the back-out path
from daily-content.md step 4. Review mode is off, so a lint-failing entry
is already on disk AND in the registry by the time the gate runs; without
these two the routine cannot undo it and the next run would commit it.
Both are scoped to src/content so neither can reach anything else.
`lint.mjs --baseline-init` is DENIED while the rest of lint.mjs is allowed.
It regenerates the grandfathered-violation baseline from scratch and cannot
tell a regression from history, so one run at the wrong moment permanently
grandfathers a brand-new violation — the exact 'never edit the baseline to
make a violation pass' rule, with a CLI flag in front of it. The routines
use --baseline-tighten, which can only remove or lower an entry. Keeping
--baseline-init a human-only command makes that structural rather than a
line of prose the model has to remember.
